items.title: Charles McPherson interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Diego, California, February 12, 1998 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: Yeah, that was the local band. In fact it was Thad Jones and Pepper Adams.

ctx.x: Yeah, that was the local band. In fact it was Thad Jones and Pepper Adams. Barry Harris was playing piano, and Elvin was the drummer, Elvin Jones. Beans Richardson I think was the bass player. And Miles would work there often. And this was the scene at this place. People like Wardell Gray would work there, because they would come in and play with the rhythm section. Billy Mitchell, Sonny Stitt. And then when people would be coming to Detroit working at other clubs, they would always come by this club, and hang…

Well nowadays we have many places you can go to school to learn jazz and so forth, and we can talk about that later, but you were sparked by that interest. So now how are you going to go about pursuing it, if you’re 14, 15?

items.title: Charles McPherson interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, September 9, 2024 [interview 2 of 2]
items.q: I just did a review on this book with Pepper Adams.

ctx.x: You mentioned of course Barry Harris, and I just did a review on this book with Pepper Adams.
